summary: I tried to refute the auditor and could not. The fix holds on the current code. The old `httpListeningLayer` sat in `Layer.mergeAll` beside `HttpRouter.serve`, so it built at the same time as serve. Commit 60633eff3 (#710) replaced it with `httpServingLayer`, which receives the serve layer through `Layer.provide`. In effect 4.0.2, `Layer.provide` (via `provideWith`) builds the provided layer fully, then builds the dependent layer. The serve layer only finishes after `HttpServer.serve` returns, and on both Node and Bun that call attaches the request/upgrade handlers synchronously at its end. So `markHttpServing`, and with it 'startup http listener ready', the `ready` publish, headless pairing output and browser open, now always follow handler attachment and the 'Listening on' log. Nothing else calls the mark; the only other `markHttpServing` references are test mocks. Desktop also treats the `http-serving` frame, written in the same post-serve layer, as its authoritative readiness signal. In 11bfda63e, Hub connector construction moved after the mark: it is forked and does not block the layer. Hub routes wait for `HubConnectorReady`, and the headless output reads the Hub origin from config only, so this does not reintroduce the race. One related point, outside the finding's scope: the proposal deliberately left `tailscaleServeLayer` concurrent. On a first boot with Tailscale Serve enabled, the headless output may probe the MagicDNS HTTPS endpoint before `ensureTailscaleServe` has finished. The link would then be left out, or a loopback-only server would print a loopback connection string. That is low value, a trade-off rather than a defect of this fix.

evidence.note: `httpServingLayer` writes the `http-serving` desktop frame, calls `startup.markHttpServing`, then forks `hubConnector.start`. A comment says it is built after `HttpRouter.serve`.

`httpServingLayer.pipe(Layer.provide(HttpRouter.serve(makeRoutesLayer,...).pipe(Layer.provideMerge(HubConnectorDeferredLive))))` is the shape the proposal asked for. `runtimeStateLayer` and `tailscaleServeLayer` stay in `mergeAll`, as the proposal said.
`provideWith` does `flatMap(that.build(...), ctx => self.build(...))`, so the dependent mark layer is built strictly after the serve layer has finished building.
`serve` builds the app layer, then `Layer.merge(HttpServer.serve(handler), ...)`, then `withLogAddress`. Its build completes only after `server.serve` returns and the address is logged.

Node `serve` calls `server.on('request'/'upgrade')` synchronously at the end of the serve effect. Bun's `BunHttpServer.ts:224-226` likewise does `handlerStack.push` plus `server.reload` synchronously.
The startup fiber awaits the `httpServing` Deferred before it logs 'startup http listener ready', publishes `ready`, prints headless output and opens the browser.

`markHttpServing` (renamed, as the proposal asked) resolves `httpServing` and releases the provider boot gate. It is the only producer; the other references are test mocks (server.test.ts:1004, threadFork.fixtures.ts:238).
Desktop treats only the `http-serving` frame, written in the post-serve layer, as authoritative backend readiness.

`start` only forks the connector build (it is not awaited in the layer), and Hub routes await `HubConnectorReady`. Moving it after the mark (11bfda63e) keeps the guarantee that requests are served or held, not dropped.

Headless output reads the Hub origin from config only, so it does not depend on the connector. It does call `registry.list`, which probes the Tailscale MagicDNS URL live (AdvertisedEndpointRegistry.ts:164-176). That is the related, out-of-scope `tailscaleServeLayer` concurrency.

fixDefects: None verified. Minor gaps: (1) No test asserts the layer ordering in server.ts, meaning that `markHttpServing` runs only after handlers are attached. A future refactor that moves `httpServingLayer` back into `mergeAll` would pass every existing test. (2) Out of scope by the proposal's own terms: `tailscaleServeLayer` still builds alongside the mark. On a first boot with `--tailscale-serve`, the headless pairing output can probe the MagicDNS HTTPS endpoint before `ensureTailscaleServe` finishes, which leaves out the Tailnet link or falls back to a loopback connection string.
implementationSketch: Optional hardening, not required to close this finding. Add a server.test.ts case that builds the `makeServerLayer` composition, or a reduced copy of it, with a stub `ServerRuntimeStartup` whose `markHttpServing` records `server.listenerCount('request') > 0`, or records the order against a fake `HttpServer.serve`. Assert that handlers were attached when the mark ran. If the Tailscale point ever matters, make the headless-output branch of the startup fiber wait for the Tailscale Serve layer: expose a Deferred, or put `tailscaleServeLayer` into the `Layer.provide` list of `httpServingLayer` so the mark follows it. Note that this delays readiness by the `tailscale` CLI call; that is a product trade-off.
decisionReason: Nothing remains for this finding. The optional Tailscale ordering tweak would trade readiness latency for pairing-output completeness, but it is out of scope.
